title: Incremental Toolproofing & SDK Ergonomics PRD (draft)
content:
Overview:
This doc proposes a cohesive approach we call 'toolproofing' — a set of streaming primitives, structured-output anchors, and SDK ergonomics that make hosted tool calls robust to partial responses, reconnects, and heterogeneous client environments. The goal is to enable app developers to compose multi-step tool flows over streaming responses with predictable correctness and low integration cost.

Why this?
- We see repeated integration issues: tool results lost on partial streams, clients unable to resume tool-handshake state, and brittle JSON parsing when the model yields mixed human-text + tool outputs.
- Existing PRDs focus on incremental framing or typed-tool contracts but don't unify runtime resume and SDK-side ergonomics. 'Toolproofing' ties them together.

Success metrics (initial):
- Reduction in reported tool-invocation flakiness in beta customers by 60%
- SDK integration time (first working tool flow) reduced from median 3 days to <8 hours
- Error class distribution: reduce 'orphan tool effects' tickets by 80%

Non-goals:
- Full language-level verification of tool semantics (out of scope)
- Replacing existing typed-tool contract surface — we build on top of it

User personas and primary flows:
1) Backend engineer wiring Redwood-hosted API to a downstream action API (e.g., create-ticket) who needs idempotent, resumable calls.
2) Mobile app developer who wants a tiny client with streaming partial previews and the ability to finalize a tool call when network is stable.
3) Platform engineer running a canary that calls tools and expects deterministic replay for debugging.

Key ideas & primitives:
- Frame Anchors: Each logical output (human text, tool call, structured object) is emitted as a self-identifying frame with an anchor id and commit status. Frames may be emitted partially and later committed.
  - Example envelope (stream): {\n    "frame_id": "f_01",\n    "type": "tool_call",\n    "tool": "issue.create",\n    "payload_partial": "{\"summary\": \"Intermitte",\n    "committed": false\n  }
  - When commit occurs we send the frame again with committed: true and final payload.

- Call Succession & Hedging: The platform may attempt speculative execution of a cheaper/approx tool variant in parallel for tail mitigation; SDKs expose a callback to receive speculative vs final results.

- Resume Tokens & Lightweight Checkpoints: For long sessions (multistep tool graphs), the runtime returns a resume token that encodes minimal session state (frame pointers + KV of tool handshakes). Clients can replay only missing frames to bring server and SDK back in sync. Tokens are opaque to SDKs but SDK helpers expose assertions.

- Deterministic Tool Effects: Tools must declare the expected side-effect idempotency level (idempotent | deduplicatable | non-idempotent). The platform enforces a minimal delivery semantics and surfaces action dedup tokens in frames.

SDK Ergonomics proposal (multi-platform):
- Tiny default: Provide a 1-file minimal adaptor for mobile/web that can: open streaming connection, buffer partial frames, emit synthetic preview events, and present a single commit API.
- Rich SDK (server/Node/python): Expose:
  - onFrame(frame) streaming callback that yields partial updates with stable frame_id, committed flag, and a schema-hint
  - commitFrame(frame_id, ack_meta) helper to mark successful local application of tool effect (sends ack to Redwood)
  - resume(session_token) to fetch missing frames and rehydrate local KV
  - speculative(handler) to receive hedged results with confidence scores

Compatibility patterns:
- Backwards compatibility: If older clients receive frames without frame_id, treat as legacy single chunk. SDK will wrap it in a synthetic frame to minimize breakage.
- Graceful degradation for low-bandwidth: frames can be compactified (delta-only) and SDK will reconstruct using last-committed anchor.

Streaming protocol sketch (HTTP/1 SSE and WebSocket variants):
- Each SSE/WS message is a JSON line with {"frame_id","type","payload_chunk","committed","sequence"}. Sequence is per-connection monotonic int used to detect gaps.
- Server side keeps a per-session ring buffer of recent frames for resume (configurable retention by SLA).
- If the client reconnects with resume_token + last_seq, server will stream missing frames and a final 'session_consistency' message indicating server-side commit watermark.

Structured output and schema reconciliation:
- We propose a lightweight schema-hint field on frames: "schema": "issue.create.v1" or a JSON-schema URL. Clients can opt-in to strict parsing or tolerant merging (attempt best-effort).
- The idea of 'frame anchors' ensures structured objects are only considered authoritative after committed=true arrives. Until then SDK exposes a preview object flagged as provisional.

Tool-handshake lifecycle (states):
- PENDING_PARTIAL: model started generating tool call payload (partial frame emitted)
- AWAITING_CONFIRM: runtime is waiting for tool execution confirmation (e.g., downstream webhook exec) — SDK may show spinner
- EXECUTED: tool returned effect/result — emitted as committed frame with effect_id and dedupe_token
- OBSOLETE: tool result superseded by a later committed frame (useful for retries/hedges)

Error semantics and developer-facing surface:
- Classification: transient (retryable), permanent (bad args/authorization), dedupe-suppressed (already applied)
- SDK receives both runtime errors and tool-side errors as frames of type 'error' with structure {"error_class":"transient","message":"...","trace_id":"..."} so debugging is alignment-friendly.

Telemetry & Observability:
- Emit events for: partial-frame-emitted, frame-committed, resume-attempt, dedupe-detected, speculative-swapped.
- Store token-level traces mapping session resume tokens to frame ids for fast customer troubleshooting in Console.

Developer UX examples (pseudo):
- Minimal Node flow:
  const conn = Redwood.stream({ model: 'rwd-13b', session_token: null })
  conn.on('frame', f => {
    if (f.type === 'tool_call') showPreview(f.payload_partial)
    if (f.committed) applyEffectLocally(f)
  })
  // on reconnect
  conn.resume(session_token).then(missing => apply(missing))

Open questions (TODOs):
- Resume token design: opaque vs signed. Tradeoffs: opaqueness reduces client surface but makes offline debugging harder.
- Retention SLA default: 5 minutes vs 1 hour for free tier. Ops impact?
- How to surface speculative hedges in billing/metrics? Count as executed tokens or not?
- Security: do we allow clients to mutate commit status via SDK? (short answer: no) but edge cases for network partitions need careful handling.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (internal experiment): implement frame-anchors in runtime + debug SDKs (server python/node) behind feature flag. 4 weeks.
- Phase 1 (beta partners): select 3 customers (customer success + solutions engineering) to try; gather integration friction metrics. 6–8 weeks.
- Phase 2 (general availability): SDKs out of beta, Console telemetry panels for frames + resume tokens, default retention SLA published. 6–10 weeks.

Risks & mitigation:
- Complexity burden on SDKs increases maintenance surface. Mitigate with a single lightweight core API and thin language wrappers.
- Misuse of speculative results leading to inconsistent application of effects. Mitigate with clear UI flags in SDKs and server-side dedupe tokens.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally high-level; next step is a companion proto and wire example (small JSON streaming harness) plus a test plan for property-based tests around resume and dedupe.
- Asking Eng-serving-runtime for an initial capacity estimate for the ring buffer storage and for SRE on retention model implications.

References and related work:
- prior PRDs on incremental output and tool-handshake (see linked artifacts)
- Conversation thread: #hosted-api-streaming on slack (https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C12345)
